text: Welcome to AI Masterclass. In this module, we'll explore a simple but important question. What is artificial intelligence? Let's start with the basics. Artificial intelligence, or AI, means computer programs that can perform tasks that normally require human thinking. These tasks include understanding language, spotting patterns, and making suggestions. You may already use AI every day without even noticing it. Your email filters spam. Your phone suggests the next word as you type. Streaming apps recommend what to watch, and maps estimate your travel time. These are examples of AI designed for specific tasks. The AI we explore in this course is different. It is a general purpose assistant. You communicate with it using normal language, and it can help you write, summarize, explain, plan, and analyze information. Let's understand three important terms. Artificial intelligence, machine learning, and large language models. AI is the big umbrella, computers performing smart tasks. Machine learning is a way of building AI where computers learn from many examples instead of being given step-by-step rules. A large language model, or LLM, is a type of machine learning model built to understand and write human language. Claude is one example. Three things came together to make modern AI possible. First, huge amounts of text became available for learning. Second, computers became much more powerful, and third, better ways of designing these systems were developed. Imagine a new colleague who has read an enormous amount, works instantly, and is happy to help with almost anything. But this colleague knows nothing about your company, your customers, or your project, until you provide that information. Sometimes they also make mistakes. Good results come from explaining things clearly and checking their work. Let's look at four common myths. First, AI thinks like a human. It doesn't. It works very differently, even if it's replies feel natural. Second, AI is just like Google. Google finds existing web pages. Claude generates a new answer each time. Third, AI is always right. It can make mistakes and still sound confident. Fourth, AI learns from me instantly. It doesn't change itself during your chat. It uses the information available in your conversation. Now, think about your own work day. Identify three tasks where you spend time writing, reading, or organizing information. These are three places where AI could potentially help. Write them down. We'll come back to them in a later module. That concludes Module 1. What is AI? In the next module, we'll explore large language models and how they generate responses. AI Masterclass, Tactive AI Team.
